# TrailFold Daypack 18L — Static Meta Creative Brief

**Purpose:** Produce three distinct static ads for the Daypack 18L. The test should learn which message earns qualified clicks without introducing unsupported product claims or increasing demand beyond available inventory.

**Inventory guardrail:** Current stock is 210 units at an observed run rate of 8 units/day—approximately 26 days of supply. Confirm the replenishment plan before scaling traffic; the stated 35-day replenishment arrival creates a potential coverage gap. Do not add a discount or make urgency claims.

## Shared production and test plan

- **Format:** One 4:5 feed asset per concept, with a 1:1 crop supplied if composition allows.
- **Brand treatment:** Restrained, useful, plain-spoken. Avoid adventure clichés, exaggerated outdoor imagery, testimonials, competitor references, waterproof language, and sustainability claims.
- **Product accuracy:** Show the Daypack 18L as the product. Water-resistant is acceptable only when stated as “water-resistant,” never “waterproof.”
- **Single variable:** Test the creative concept/message only. Hold audience, campaign objective, placements, landing page, attribution settings, optimization event, and spend allocation constant. Use one final asset per concept; do not add headline or image variants during the initial read.
- **Measurement:** Review outbound CTR, landing-page view rate, add-to-cart rate, checkout starts, purchases, and cost per purchase. Treat Meta-reported purchase value as directional because it is not reconciled to Shopify. Do not declare a winner from CTR alone.
- **Inventory rule:** Keep the test controlled and pause before scaling if demand materially exceeds the owner-approved stock plan.

## Concept 1 — Desk-to-trail iteration

**Hypothesis:** Showing one bag moving between weekday work and a short weekend outing will make the product’s practical versatility immediately clear.

**Headline:** “One bag for workdays and short weekends.”

**Body:** “The Daypack 18L keeps the daily carry straightforward: a padded 13-inch laptop sleeve, external bottle pocket, and water-resistant fabric. Free US shipping.”

**CTA:** “Shop Daypack 18L”

**Image composition:** Split-scene or visual transition from a clean desk on the left to a simple park or trail setting on the right. Keep the same bag prominent in both settings. Include restrained labels such as “Workday” and “Weekend,” but do not imply technical outdoor performance.

**Production instructions:** Use neutral colors, natural light, and minimal props. Make the bag large enough to identify on mobile. Add a small footer: “Water-resistant, not waterproof.” Confirm the legal/product copy remains legible in the 4:5 crop.

## Concept 2 — Laptop-fit objection

**Hypothesis:** Addressing laptop uncertainty directly will improve qualified clicks from shoppers who are deciding whether the Daypack works for their device.

**Headline:** “15-inch laptop? Don’t guess.”

**Body:** “The Daypack has a padded sleeve designed for a 13-inch laptop. If you carry a 15-inch model, check your laptop and sleeve dimensions on the product page before ordering.”

**CTA:** “Check the fit”

**Image composition:** Product shown open beside a laptop, with a clean measurement-focused layout. Do not show a 15-inch laptop inserted or imply that it fits. Reserve a clearly marked area for verified sleeve dimensions once supplied.

**Production instructions:** Use a simple diagram or ruler graphic only if the measurements are verified. Until then, use the open-bag visual without numeric dimension callouts. Keep the warning prominent but not alarmist.

## Concept 3 — Fresh positioning hypothesis: practical carry

**Hypothesis:** Positioning the bag as an uncomplicated daily tool—not an adventure statement—will attract commuters who also take short trips.

**Headline:** “Carry what the day actually needs.”

**Body:** “An 18L daypack for commutes and short weekend trips, with a padded 13-inch laptop sleeve and external bottle pocket. Plain, practical, ready for the next stop.”

**CTA:** “See the Daypack”

**Image composition:** Front-facing product on a real commuter setup: laptop, notebook, bottle, and compact personal items arranged neatly beside it. Avoid showing more contents than the 18L capacity can reasonably support.

**Production instructions:** Use a warm neutral background and straightforward product labeling. No mountains, extreme weather, or aspirational lifestyle treatment. Keep the Daypack as the visual focus.

**Designer allocation:** Concept 1: 2.5 hours; Concept 2: 2.5 hours; Concept 3: 3 hours. **Total: 8 hours.**
